title: Cloud Provider API Rate Limit Monitoring

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.30 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.30 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via Cloud TAs + application logs with HTTP status; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Cloud TAs + application logs with HTTP status

description: Automation hitting AWS throttling, Azure 429s, or GCP RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED breaks pipelines; trending limits prevents silent job loss.
value: Detecting cloud provider api rate limit monitoring early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Cloud TAs + application logs with HTTP status with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Back off and jitter in automation based on Splunk alerts. Separate control-plane vs data-plane APIs. Dashboard top callers (principal or workload) causing throttles.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (  errorCode="Throttling")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.30_cloud_provider_api_rate_30"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect cloud provider api rate limit monitoring. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_30_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (throttle count by provider), Table (API operation, caller, count), Single value (15m throttle burst)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Cloud TAs + application logs with HTTP status and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud provider api rate limit monitoring so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
